findings.title: $__range queries are now split because the range check runs after interpolation
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() (line 287) exists so that queries containing $__range are not split, because $__range has to be evaluated against the full time range of the request. Before this change it saw the raw expression. Now runSplitQuery interpolates first (line 299) and partitions on the result (line 300). Any $__range that applyTemplateVariables resolves from request.scopedVars (Grafana supplies __range for panel queries) has already been replaced by a literal, so isQueryWithRangeVariable() returns false and the query is split. Each time chunk then runs with the full-range literal as its window and combineResponses merges the chunks, which gives wrong results for range aggregations. No test in the PR covers this exclusion.

findings.title: Shard path no longer drops targets whose expression interpolates to empty
findings.body: The old code interpolated first and then filtered on expr, so a target whose expression is a variable expanding to an empty string was dropped. The filter now runs on the raw expression (line 50), before the map on line 52, so such targets survive. They are passed to runSplitQuery as a subrequest, where the empty expr is filtered out (querySplitting.ts line 298). If nothing is left, runSplitGroupedQueries reads requests.filter(...)[0].partition (querySplitting.ts line 96) on an empty array and throws a TypeError. On the sharded path that throw happens inside the groupTargetsByQueryType().then() callback, so the rejection is unhandled and the observable never emits. For example, a panel with a metric query plus a query like $q, where $q is empty, would hang instead of returning the metric results.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation, so expressions that expand to empty are not dropped
findings.body: The filter on line 298 checks query.expr before applyTemplateVariables runs on line 299. A target such as $query whose variable expands to an empty string passes the filter and goes to runQuery with an empty expr, which the backend will reject. If that target is the only one, the requests array ends up empty and runSplitGroupedQueries throws a TypeError at line 96. The empty check should run after the interpolation step, as the old shard code did.

findings.title: Targets are interpolated twice on the sharded path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) already calls applyTemplateVariables on every target. Each shard subrequest is then passed to runSplitQuery, which calls applyTemplateVariables again on the already expanded expression (line 299) with the same scopedVars and filters. Expansion is not idempotent: if a variable value contains a $name token that matches a template variable, it gets expanded a second time and the query changes. The test change shows the redundancy: 'Interpolates queries before running' went from toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) to toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5), which codifies the repeated calls instead of removing them. Interpolation should happen once per request, with the sharded path skipping the second pass.

findings.title: Ad-hoc filters are now passed on the sharded path and then applied again per subrequest
findings.body: The removed call interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars) did not pass request.filters. The new applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) does. The subRequest built at line 154 keeps the original request's filters, so runSplitQuery applies them again (querySplitting.ts line 299). If applyTemplateVariables applies ad-hoc filters to the expression, sharded queries get the filter matchers added twice, and that behavior change is not covered by any test, because the mock in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts ignores the third argument.

findings.title: New interpolation test checks only runQuery arguments, not the splitting decisions
findings.body: The added test asserts only the expr and step passed to runQuery. The point of the fix for #107530 is that interpolated values drive splitting: calculateStep reads query.step (used for metric partitioning) and querySupportsSplitting reads the expression. Nothing checks that a $step value changes the metric stepMs grouping, or that a $__range query is excluded from splitting after interpolation.
